# Ticket 1 — Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

### Blocked by
—

### Description
The server can already remember, list and forget Claude accounts (`ClaudeAccounts` in `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts`), but no client can reach it. This ticket makes those three operations callable over T3's WebSocket RPC, from the web and desktop app, locally and remotely. It moves the account schemas and the account error into `packages/contracts` and rewrites every error message in plain words, with no internal setup ID and no command line in it. Later tickets build the screens on this.

No screen changes in this ticket. Switching (ticket 2) and adding an account (ticket 3) come later.

### Acceptance criteria
Scenario AK-14: Remembering the logged-in account from the Claude provider settings
  Given a Claude setup logged in with an account T3 has not remembered yet
  When the user chooses to remember it in the Claude provider settings and names it "Work"
  Then the account is remembered as "Work"
  And the settings list "Work" as the active account
Serves: R6

Scenario AK-25: Settings list the remembered accounts and mark the active one
  Given a Claude setup logged in as "Work" with "Work" and "Private" remembered
  When the user opens the Claude provider settings
  Then they see "Work" and "Private" listed
  And "Work" is marked as active
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-28: Confirming forget removes the account from the list
  Given the user has been asked to confirm forgetting "Private"
  When they confirm
  Then "Private" is no longer listed
  And "Private" is no longer offered for switching in the model picker
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-30: Forgetting the active account keeps the setup logged in
  Given a Claude setup logged in as the remembered account "Work"
  When the user forgets "Work" and confirms
  Then the setup is still logged in with that account
  And the account is shown as not remembered, with the offer to remember it
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-36: The desktop app connected remotely lists the remote setup's accounts
  Given the desktop app connected to a T3 on another machine whose Claude setup has "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  When the user opens the Claude provider settings
  Then they see "Work" and "Private" listed
  And "Work" is marked as active
Serves: R13

This ticket proves the server side of these scenarios, through the RPC boundary that a client uses. The screens that show the result, the confirmation dialogs and the offer to remember come in ticket 4 (settings) and ticket 5 (model picker). They consume the RPCs defined here.

### Test specification
Unit (`packages/contracts/src/claudeAccounts.test.ts`, new):
- For every literal in `ClaudeAccountErrorReason`, a `ClaudeAccountError` built with `instanceId: "claudeAgent_work"` and `name: "Work"` has a non-empty `message`. The message contains none of: `claudeAgent_work`, a backtick, `claude auth`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. (Proves the plain-language rule for every reason, including ones that tickets 2 and 3 will add.)
- A `ClaudeAccountError({ reason: "nameInUse", name: "Work" })` that is encoded with `Schema.encodeUnknownSync(ClaudeAccountError)` and decoded again with `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(ClaudeAccountError)` keeps its `reason`, its `name` and the same `message`. This shows the client rebuilds the same text.

Integration (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts`, new `describe("over the WebSocket RPC")` that reuses the file's existing harness: temp setup dirs, real `ServerSecretStore`, pinned `HostProcess`). The RPCs run through `RpcServer.makeNoSerialization` over `RpcGroup.make(WsClaudeAccountsListRpc, WsClaudeAccountsRememberRpc, WsClaudeAccountsForgetRpc)`, with handlers from `claudeAccountsRpcHandlers` and the real `ClaudeAccounts` layer, the same way `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts:602-631` drives Rpcs:
- AK-14: setup `claudeAgent` is logged in as an account that is not remembered. `claudeAccounts.remember { instanceId: "claudeAgent", name: "Work" }` returns `{ name: "Work", email }`. A following `claudeAccounts.list` shows the setup with `active.rememberedAs === "Work"`.
- AK-25 / AK-36: "Work" and "Private" are remembered and the setup is logged in as Work. `claudeAccounts.list` returns both names in `accounts`, and the setup's `active.rememberedAs` is `"Work"`.
- AK-28: after `claudeAccounts.forget { name: "Private" }`, `claudeAccounts.list` no longer contains "Private" in `accounts`.
- AK-30: after `claudeAccounts.forget { name: "Work" }` while Work is active, the setup's `.credentials.json` and `.claude.json` are byte-identical to before. `claudeAccounts.list` shows the setup with `active.email` unchanged and `active.rememberedAs === null`.
- A refused call reaches the caller as a typed failure. `claudeAccounts.remember` with a name already in use fails with `ClaudeAccountError` reason `nameInUse`, and its `message` contains no setup ID. With `HostProcess.Platform` set to `"darwin"`, `claudeAccounts.list` fails with reason `unavailable`.

Existing tests that must keep passing unchanged in their assertions: `apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.test.ts` (one scope per Rpc) and `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts` (it gains one `Layer.mock(ClaudeAccounts.ClaudeAccounts)({})` entry in its mock wall, because `layerWsRpc` now yields the service). The existing `ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts` assertions that pin the old `needsFreshLogin` and `switchRollbackFailed` texts (`:1374`, `:2214`) are updated to the new texts below. That is a required behaviour change (R11), and the hand-off must justify it.

Boundaries doubled: the Claude login check (`ClaudeLoginCheck`, already scripted in the harness), the `/proc` scan (fake proc root, already in the harness) and the host process (`HostProcess.*`, pinned). Everything else is real: secret store, settings service, SQLite in memory, the RPC server.

e2e: none. There is no e2e suite, and the integration tests above stand in for it. The screens are proven in tickets 4 and 5.

### Design reference


### Implementation details
Module: `packages/contracts` (wire types), `apps/server` (RPC handlers), `packages/client-runtime` (client atoms)

Files:
- [NEW] `packages/contracts/src/claudeAccounts.ts` — the Claude account wire types and error, moved from the server.
- [MODIFY] `packages/contracts/src/index.ts` — add `export * from "./claudeAccounts.ts";` next to `./providerSetup.ts`.
- [NEW] `packages/contracts/src/claudeAccounts.test.ts` — the unit tests above.
- [MODIFY] `packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts` — three `WS_METHODS` entries, three `Rpc.make` declarations, and their listing in `WsRpcGroup`.
- [MODIFY] `packages/contracts/src/clientRpcPermissions.ts` — guard remember and forget with `AuthProvidersManageScope`.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts` — delete the local schema and error definitions, import them from `@t3tools/contracts`, and re-export them, so existing imports of `./ClaudeAccounts.ts` keep working.
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccountsRpc.ts` — the handler functions over the service.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/ws.ts` — yield the service in `layerWsRpc` and spread the handlers into `ServerWsRpcGroup.of({...})`.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts` — a required scope for the three methods.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/observability/RpcInstrumentation.ts` — span area `"provider"` for the three methods.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts` — add `Layer.mock(ClaudeAccounts.ClaudeAccounts)({})` to the mock wall.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts` — the RPC describe block, and the two updated message assertions.
- [MODIFY] `packages/client-runtime/src/state/server.ts` — the client query and commands.

Consumes: nothing from earlier tickets. From the repository: `ClaudeAccounts` service (`remember`, `list`, `forget`), `ProviderInstanceId`, `EnvironmentAuthorizationError`, `AuthProvidersManageScope`, `AuthOrchestrationReadScope`.

Produces (exact names, used by tickets 2–6):
- In `@t3tools/contracts` (`claudeAccounts.ts`):
  - `ClaudeAccountErrorReason` — `Schema.Literals([...])` with the 17 existing reasons, unchanged in name and order.
  - `ClaudeAccountError` — `Schema.TaggedError<ClaudeAccountError>()("ClaudeAccountError", { reason: ClaudeAccountErrorReason, instanceId: Schema.optional(ProviderInstanceId), name: Schema.optional(Schema.String) })`, with the `message` getter below.
  - `RememberedClaudeAccount` — `Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.String, email: Schema.String })`.
  - `ClaudeSetupAccountState` — `Schema.Struct({ instanceId: ProviderInstanceId, displayName: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String), active: Schema.NullOr(Schema.Struct({ email: Schema.String, rememberedAs: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String) })) })`.
  - `ClaudeAccountList` — `Schema.Struct({ accounts: Schema.Array(RememberedClaudeAccount), setups: Schema.Array(ClaudeSetupAccountState) })`.
  - `ClaudeSwitchResult` — `Schema.Struct({ instanceId: ProviderInstanceId, active: RememberedClaudeAccount, affectedInstanceIds: Schema.Array(ProviderInstanceId) })`. It moves now, because it sits in the same block. Ticket 2 puts it on the wire.
  - `ClaudeAccountListInput` — `Schema.Struct({})`.
  - `ClaudeAccountRememberInput` — `Schema.Struct({ instanceId: ProviderInstanceId, name: Schema.String })`.
  - `ClaudeAccountForgetInput` — `Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.String })`.
  - Each schema also exports its `type X = typeof X.Type`, as the server file does today.
- In `packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts`:
  - `WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsList = "claudeAccounts.list"`, `WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsRemember = "claudeAccounts.remember"`, `WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsForget = "claudeAccounts.forget"`.
  - `ClaudeAccountRpcError = Schema.Union([ClaudeAccountError, EnvironmentAuthorizationError])`, exported for tickets 2 and 3.
  - `WsClaudeAccountsListRpc` (payload `ClaudeAccountListInput`, success `ClaudeAccountList`), `WsClaudeAccountsRememberRpc` (payload `ClaudeAccountRememberInput`, success `RememberedClaudeAccount`) and `WsClaudeAccountsForgetRpc` (payload `ClaudeAccountForgetInput`, success `Schema.Void`). All three use error `ClaudeAccountRpcError`, and all three are exported so the integration test can build its group.
- In `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccountsRpc.ts`: `export const claudeAccountsRpcHandlers = (accounts: ClaudeAccounts["Service"]) => ({ [WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsList]: (_input: ClaudeAccountListInput) => accounts.list, [WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsRemember]: (input: ClaudeAccountRememberInput) => accounts.remember(input), [WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsForget]: (input: ClaudeAccountForgetInput) => accounts.forget(input) })`. Tickets 2 and 3 add their handlers to this same object.
- In `packages/client-runtime/src/state/server.ts`, inside `createServerEnvironmentAtoms`:
  - `claudeAccountList: createEnvironmentRpcQueryAtomFamily(runtime, { label: "environment-data:claude-accounts:list", tag: WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsList })`.
  - `rememberClaudeAccount: createEnvironmentRpcCommand(runtime, { label: "environment-data:claude-accounts:remember", tag: WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsRemember })`.
  - `forgetClaudeAccount: createEnvironmentRpcCommand(runtime, { label: "environment-data:claude-accounts:forget", tag: WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsForget })`.
  - The web reads them as `serverEnvironment.claudeAccountList`, `serverEnvironment.rememberClaudeAccount` and `serverEnvironment.forgetClaudeAccount`, with targets `{ environmentId, input }`.

Scopes:
- `claudeAccountsList` → `AuthOrchestrationReadScope`. The same account email already reaches every reader through the provider snapshot (`ServerProviderAuth.email`), and the model picker must show the account to any session that can see the composer.
- `claudeAccountsRemember` and `claudeAccountsForget` → `AuthProvidersManageScope`, the scope of every other provider credential mutation (`providerAuthStart`, `providerAuthLogout`). Both are also listed in `CLIENT_GUARDED_RPC_SCOPES` as `[WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsRemember]: AuthProvidersManageScope` and `[WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsForget]: AuthProvidersManageScope`, so screens can read `serverEnvironment.rememberClaudeAccount.permissionAtom(environmentId)` (AGENTS.md rule for new guarded mutations).

Error messages: the `message` getter moves into contracts with these exact texts, each a JavaScript template where `${this.name}` appears:
- `unavailable`: "Switching Claude accounts is only supported when T3 runs on Linux."
- `setupNotFound`: "This Claude setup no longer exists."
- `setupUnreadable`: "T3 could not read the login of this Claude setup."
- `notLoggedIn`: "No Claude account is logged in on this Claude setup."
- `invalidName`: "An account name must be 1 to 64 characters long and contain no control characters." (unchanged)
- `nameInUse`: `The name "${this.name}" is already in use.` (unchanged)
- `alreadyRemembered`: `This account is already remembered as "${this.name}".` (unchanged)
- `accountNotFound`: `No remembered Claude account is named "${this.name}".` (unchanged)
- `storage`: "Could not read or save the remembered Claude accounts." (unchanged)
- `currentNotRemembered`: "The account logged in on this Claude setup is not remembered yet. Remember it first, then switch."
- `needsFreshLogin`: `The saved login of "${this.name}" no longer works. Forget "${this.name}", then add it again.`
- `loginCheckFailed`: `Could not check the saved login of "${this.name}". Try again.` (unchanged)
- `switchFailed`: "Switching failed. The Claude setup is still logged in as before."
- `switchRollbackFailed`: "Switching failed and the Claude setup's login could not be restored. Log in to this Claude setup again."
- `externalClaudePrograms`: "Claude programs started outside T3 are using this Claude setup. Close them, then switch again."
- `processCheckFailed`: "T3 could not check whether Claude programs started outside T3 are using this Claude setup. Try again."
- `sessionStopFailed`: "T3 could not stop the running turns on this Claude setup. It is still logged in as before. Try again."

`instanceId` stays a field on the error for logs and for clients that want to point at the setup. The text no longer contains it.

Decisions:
- Handlers live in a small `ClaudeAccountsRpc.ts` and are spread into `ws.ts`, instead of being written inline there. This lets the integration test drive the real handlers with the real service and the existing temp-dir harness, without building the whole `layerWsRpc` mock wall. The cost is that one area of handlers sits outside `ws.ts`. The handlers stay one-line delegations, as AGENTS.md:154 asks.
- The schemas move to contracts and are re-exported from `ClaudeAccounts.ts`, not duplicated. One definition crosses the wire, and the 2216-line integration test keeps its imports. The cost is a re-export line in the server module.
- The messages carry no setup ID. They say "this Claude setup", because every place that shows them (picker row, setup card, add dialog) already sits on one setup. The cost: a log line that only has the message loses the ID, but `instanceId` stays on the error and in the existing structured log fields.
- `needsFreshLogin` now points to the in-app way out (forget, then add again; adding comes in ticket 3) instead of a CLI command. The cost: until ticket 3 lands, that advice names a button that does not exist yet. Both tickets ship in the same Auftrag.

Handler wiring in `ws.ts`: at the top of `layerWsRpc`, next to `const providerAuth = yield* ProviderAuthService.ProviderAuthService;` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1279`), add `const claudeAccounts = yield* ClaudeAccounts.ClaudeAccounts;` (with `import * as ClaudeAccounts from "./provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts";` and `import { claudeAccountsRpcHandlers } from "./provider/ClaudeAccountsRpc.ts";`). Inside `ServerWsRpcGroup.of({...})` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1806`), add `...claudeAccountsRpcHandlers(claudeAccounts),`. No error mapping is needed, because the service already fails with the wire type `ClaudeAccountError`. No new layer wiring is needed, because `ClaudeAccounts` already reaches `layerWsRpc` through `layerProduction` (`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.ts:396`).

Consumers updated by the contracts change: `apps/server` (handlers, scope map, instrumentation map) and `packages/client-runtime` (atoms). `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and `apps/mobile` need no change: `RpcClient.make(WsRpcGroup)` picks up the new tags (`packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:5`). The mobile app is out of scope and gets no screen.

Deliberately left out: the switch RPC (ticket 2), the add-account login (ticket 3), and every screen (tickets 4–6). There is no capability flag for "accounts supported" in `ExecutionEnvironmentCapabilities`. Clients gate on `ServerConfig.environment.platform.os === "linux"`, and the server refuses with `unavailable` anywhere else.

| Criterion | Requirement | Exists in Auftrag, text matches | What this ticket proves | End to end in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AK-14 | R6 (remember the unremembered account) | yes | remember RPC, then list shows `rememberedAs` | ticket 4 |
| AK-25 | R10 (list, mark active) | yes | list RPC returns both, active marked | ticket 4 |
| AK-28 | R10 (forget after confirm) | yes | forget RPC removes from list | ticket 4 (settings), ticket 5 (picker clause) |
| AK-30 | R10 (forget active keeps login) | yes | credential files byte-identical, `rememberedAs` null | ticket 4 |

## Findings

**[suggestion] focus-1 — The message rewrite serves R11, but the ticket cites no R11 criterion**
**Where:** §Description, "rewrites every error message in plain words"; §Implementation details, "Error messages"
**Evidence:** Auftrag R11 ("When T3 refuses an action, the user sees the reason in plain words") and its criterion AK-31; the ticket names R11 only in §Test specification, "That is a required behaviour change (R11)"
**Why:** the largest behaviour change in the ticket is missing from its criteria list, so the Coverage check cannot see that R11's message rule lands here while AK-31 itself lands with the switch.
**Taken or declined when:** §Acceptance criteria names R11 as served by the message texts and says which ticket proves AK-31 end to end.

**[suggestion] focus-2 — AK-36's remote clause has no proof of its own**
**Where:** §Test specification, "AK-25 / AK-36"
**Evidence:** AK-36 "the desktop app connected to a T3 on another machine"; the test drives the same in-process RPC as AK-25
**Why:** the test proves the list, not the remote path, so AK-36 reads as covered here while its distinguishing clause is untested.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket says AK-36 is proven here only as far as AK-25 is, and names the ticket that proves the remote connection.

## Out of lens
gremium-security: `claudeAccountsList` under `AuthOrchestrationReadScope` exposes remembered account names and emails to every reader; the ticket justifies it, the seat should weigh it.
0 blockers, 2 suggestions. The ticket traces to R6, R10 and R13 cleanly; it leaves R11 and the remote clause of AK-36 implicit.

# Pragmatist — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

## Findings

**[blocker] pragmatist-1 — The message rewrite serves R11, whose criteria belong to tickets 2 and 3**
**Where:** ticket §Description, "rewrites every error message in plain words"; §Implementation details, "Error messages"; §Test specification, the two updated assertions at `:1374`, `:2214`
**Evidence:** R11 is served by AK-31 (refused switch) and AK-32 (refused add-account) in the Auftrag; this ticket lists neither. Seven of the rewritten reasons (`currentNotRemembered`, `needsFreshLogin`, `switchFailed`, `switchRollbackFailed`, `externalClaudePrograms`, `processCheckFailed`, `sessionStopFailed`) only arise on `switch`, which this ticket does not expose. §Decisions admits the new `needsFreshLogin` text names a button that does not exist yet.
**Why:** the switch-message change could be accepted or rejected on its own, and it changes existing switch-test assertions in a ticket about list, remember and forget.
**Closes when:** the ticket moves the error class with its current texts and rewrites only the reasons that `list`, `remember` and `forget` can return. The switch texts and the two assertion updates move to ticket 2 under AK-31. Alternatively, the ticket names the criterion of its own that requires the full rewrite.

**[suggestion] pragmatist-2 — `ClaudeSwitchResult` moves without a consumer in this ticket**
**Where:** §Produces, "It moves now, because it sits in the same block. Ticket 2 puts it on the wire."
**Evidence:** no RPC in this ticket returns it.
**Why:** ticket 2 needs it, so ticket 2 can move it with the switch RPC. That keeps this diff to what its criteria use.
**Taken or declined when:** the schema moves in ticket 2, or the ticket says why it must move now.

**[suggestion] pragmatist-3 — New guarded methods skip the permission behaviour tests that AGENTS.md asks for**
**Where:** §Implementation details, `clientRpcPermissions.ts` entry; §Test specification
**Evidence:** AGENTS.md:153: "extend the permission behavior tests when adding a protected method".
**Why:** the ticket follows half of the convention for guarded mutations and leaves the test half out without saying why.
**Taken or declined when:** the test specification names the permission test it extends, or says why none applies.
Round 1:  1 blockers, 2 suggestions. The message rewrite for switch errors serves R11, whose criteria belong to tickets 2 and 3, not this one.

# Solutions Architect — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

## Findings

**[suggestion] architect-1 — The list query has no stated refresh path after remember or forget**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, Produces, `claudeAccountList: createEnvironmentRpcQueryAtomFamily(...)`
**Evidence:** fact #78, #115: query families cache per target; `createEnvironmentRpcQueryAtomFamily` takes `refreshTrigger`/`staleTimeMs` (packages/client-runtime/src/state/runtime.ts:752-780); the ticket sets neither, and AK-28 needs "Private is no longer listed"
**Why:** tickets 4 and 5 consume this atom by name; if it does not refresh after `rememberClaudeAccount`/`forgetClaudeAccount` (or after a switch in ticket 2), each screen will invent its own refresh and the contract tickets 4–5 build on is decided implicitly.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket says how `claudeAccountList` is refreshed after its own mutations (refreshTrigger, explicit `refresh`, or left to the screens — stated).

**[suggestion] architect-2 — Client gating on `platform.os === "linux"` couples clients to a server implementation detail; the cost is not named**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, "Deliberately left out", the sentence "Clients gate on `ServerConfig.environment.platform.os === "linux"`"
**Evidence:** fact #72 (no capability flag exists, `ExecutionEnvironmentCapabilities` is where feature flags live), fact #73 (OS-gating precedent), fact #3 (Linux-only is a `requireLinux` check inside the service)
**Why:** the decision names no alternative and no cost: if the server ever lifts `requireLinux`, every client check has to change, whereas a capability flag would move with the server.
**Taken or declined when:** the decision names the capability-flag alternative and what the OS check gives up, or picks the flag.

**[suggestion] architect-3 — Two sources for "the active account" with no stated owner**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, Produces, `ClaudeSetupAccountState.active.email`; §Scopes, "The same account email already reaches every reader through the provider snapshot"
**Evidence:** fact #64 (snapshot `auth.email` is published and pushed via `providerStatuses`, fact #62); fact #9 (`list` computes `active` from the login files on each call)
**Why:** later tickets will show the active account from one of two places that can disagree (pushed, cached up to 5 min per fact #65, vs. pulled on demand); naming now which one screens read for "active" keeps tickets 4–5 from choosing differently.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket states which of the two the screens treat as the active account, or defers it to ticket 4 explicitly.

## Out of lens
gremium-security: the RPC integration tests run a bare `RpcGroup.make(...)` via `makeNoSerialization` without `RpcScopeAuthorization`, so the chosen scopes are proven only by the map's completeness check, not by a refused call.
Round 1: 0 blockers, 3 suggestions. The produced client contract leaves refresh, platform gating and the source of the active account for later tickets to decide implicitly.

# Security — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

## Findings

**[blocker] security-1 — `claudeAccounts.list` gives read-only sessions the email of every remembered account**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, Scopes, "`claudeAccountsList` → `AuthOrchestrationReadScope`. The same account email already reaches every reader…"
**Evidence:** fact #64: the provider snapshot publishes only the *active* login's email; fact #9 and #18: `list` returns all remembered accounts globally, each with `email`. `packages/contracts/src/auth.ts` lets a grant be narrowed to explicit scopes, so a session with `orchestration:read` and without `providers:manage` exists.
**Why:** the rationale is wrong for every non-active account: a narrowed read-only session newly learns the emails of all accounts the owner has remembered, across every setup — personal data moved to a wider audience without the ticket saying so.
**Closes when:** the ticket either puts `list` (or the `email` of non-active accounts) behind `AuthProvidersManageScope`, or names this exposure as a deliberate choice with a reason the Purpose supports, and the test specification proves whichever rule it picks.

**[blocker] security-2 — No test proves the scope of the three new methods**
**Where:** ticket §Test specification — the RPC tests run through `RpcServer.makeNoSerialization` without `RpcAuthorization`, and `RpcAuthorization.test.ts` stays "unchanged in its assertions"
**Evidence:** fact #44: that test only checks every Rpc has *some* scope; the same file already pins specific mappings per method (e.g. webhook delivery logs → operate, relay read vs write) with `requiredScopeForRpcMethod`.
**Why:** remember and forget mutate stored OAuth logins (fact #16); a mapping typed as `AuthOrchestrationReadScope` by mistake would compile, pass every listed test and let any reader forget accounts.
**Closes when:** the test specification adds assertions that remember and forget require `AuthProvidersManageScope` and list requires the scope security-1 settles on, in `RpcAuthorization.test.ts` alongside the existing per-method cases.

**[suggestion] security-3 — Assert that no login data crosses the RPC boundary**
**Where:** ticket §Test specification, Integration
**Evidence:** fact #53: the harness already has `assertNoLogin`; fact #17: tokens are `Redacted` in the service.
**Why:** the schemas now cross the wire for the first time; one cheap assertion over every RPC success and failure body proves no token or path leaks through encoding.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket states whether the RPC describe block runs `assertNoLogin` over the encoded responses and errors.

**[suggestion] security-4 — Declare the remember/forget scopes once**
**Where:** ticket §Files, `RpcAuthorization.ts` "a required scope for the three methods", and §Scopes, `CLIENT_GUARDED_RPC_SCOPES`
**Evidence:** fact #47: `CLIENT_GUARDED_RPC_SCOPES` is spread into `RPC_REQUIRED_SCOPES`.
**Why:** writing remember and forget in both maps creates two copies of the same control that can drift; a later explicit key silently overrides the spread one.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket says `RpcAuthorization.ts` gains only the `claudeAccountsList` entry.

**[suggestion] security-5 — Bound `name` in the wire schema**
**Where:** ticket §Produces, `ClaudeAccountRememberInput` and `ClaudeAccountForgetInput`, `name: Schema.String`
**Evidence:** fact #8: the service enforces 1–64 characters only after decoding.
**Why:** a length check at the schema refuses an oversized name at the RPC boundary before it reaches the service, its logs (fact #17 logs the name) or an error message that echoes it.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket states whether the input schemas carry a maximum length.
Round 1:  2 blockers, 3 suggestions. The access rule for the new methods is wrong for list and proven for none.

# API contract — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

## Findings
